sentences.text: Neutral Citation No. - 2023:AHC:112553 Court No. - 82 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 2289 of 2023 Applicant :- Dev Dutt Sharma

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohd. Ashraf Abbasi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.544 of 2022, under sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 I.P.C, Police Station Kotwali, District Bareilly.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that in this case, he was seller of the land which was agreed to be sold in favour of the informant regarding which Rs.16,00,000/- were transferred in the account of the present applicant and agreement was made to execute the sale deed.

Later on, time was said to be extended for execution of sale deed and allegedly Rs.

1 20,00,000/- were taken by the present applicant in cash regarding which there is nothing on record to show that the said amount was handed over to the present applicant by the informant.

entities.text: Dev Dutt Sharma vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that later on, the sale deed could not be executed in favour of the informant by the present applicant and the amount of Rs.16,00,000/- were again transferred in the account of the informant which is admitted.
No money in cash was given to the applicant, therefore, there was no question to return him Rs.20,00,000/- said to be given in cash.

It is further submitted that only for the purpose of making harassment of the applicant, the present F.I.R was lodged with false allegation and investigation is going on, as a result the applicant is under apprehension of arrest by the police, so request for anticipatory bail.
Learned A.G.A opposed the prayer as aforesaid.

On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A and perusal of record, it appears that the money which was transferred in the account of the applicant was repaid and without making any further comment on the merit of the case and considering the nature of accusation and his antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
In the event of arrest of the applicant-Dev Dutt Sharma, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.
25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police office as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
